report:
Held-out round 3, processes.md and binaries.md. Result: 15 failures, all instances of known classes, none proposes a new MUST, no new class.

Scope. 60 distinct cells (36 Verification-column `rg`/script spans extracted mechanically from the two files, P1-P16 including both P4 lines, G1-G4, canary, pin jq, triangulate.py) were run verbatim, with the shipped `seams()` P0 defined, under bash on the 4 trees at 2 scopes each: product dir (`src/Markdig`, `src/CsvHelper`, `src/CommandLineUtils`, `src`) and whole tree (`SRC=.`). That is 240 cell-tree runs; the copies are in fixtures/heldout3-procbin/, outputs in _run/out/. The two analyzer-build cells were also run: I installed the shipped BannedSymbols.txt and BannedSymbols.Src.txt plus BannedApiAnalyzers 5.6.0 on a copy of CommandLineUtils (net8.0 leg) and on markdig's tools/GfmTableDifferential (net10.0), and counted the RS0030 diagnostics. Two further checks used synthetic inputs: P13 shape variants, and triangulate.py with poisoned inputs. A second, independent grep for the family's subjects (child-process launch, Arguments, Kill, WaitForExit, ReadToEnd, encodings, env, signal handlers, CancelAfter, HttpClient, certificate callbacks, hash compares) found no launch site or violation that P0 and the cells did not also see. The canary and pin cells were run with unset and bogus operands and print their MISSING messages.

Trees. Only 2 of the 4 launch children; the other 2 are out of scope by tag and every PROC cell is empty on them.
- CsvHelper: no launch. PROC cells all empty. BIN cells only noise from the docs generator (File.WriteAllText, CreateDirectory) in the whole-tree scope.
- Ocelot (API gateway, no launch): PROC empty except `CancelAfter` in two gateway handlers (src, c13). BIN cells print noise only (c23 9/69, c34 5/34, c35 12/46 for src/all), none relevant to a binary downloader.
- markdig: the only launches are tools/GfmTableDifferential (2 sites in 1 file, a dev oracle harness). Whole-tree hits: c02 1, c09 1, c18 2, P3 1, P9 2, P16 1. The product library hits only c29 (5 false positives).
- CommandLineUtils: the only launching library. `Pager.cs` starts `less`; two doc samples start a user-chosen program. Hits: c02 3 lines, P3 1, P9 4 (Pager.cs) + 12 (samples), P16 2 + 4, G4 empty sections. RS0030 on Pager.cs: Kill() line 101, ProcessStartInfo.Arguments line 123, WaitForExit() line 174. Plus Console.CancelKeyPress x3 in PhysicalConsole.cs and SecureString x6 in Prompt.cs.

Hits read and judged. true-positive-by-letter: c02 on `FileName = "less"` and `new ProcessStartInfo("git")`; P3 on Pager (the only harmless one, the pager is disabled on Windows); P9/P16 on Pager and the markdig tool; c18 on the markdig tool; RS0030 on ReadToEnd/WaitForExit in the tool. False positive: c09 (`StandardOutputEncoding = Encoding.UTF8`, the BOM hazard exists only on the input side); c29 (5 hits). Test-project noise in the Ocelot whole-tree scope (c13 and P8 in unit/acceptance dirs, c23/c34/c35 in unit/acceptance/testing).

Rule fitness (real, well-run code that breaks a rule for a good reason; findings F1-F5): CommandLineUtils `Pager.cs` is an interactive, optional, PATH-resolved child. It inherits stdout and stderr on purpose (PROC-02 demands all three redirected), starts the bare name `less` (PROC-03 resolver, BIN-01), waits unbounded for a human with sync `WaitForExit()` (PROC-09 and PROC-15 forbid it), swallows every start failure to degrade to the console (PROC-05), and exposes a public `Kill()`. No row names a sanctioned form. The `[cli-wrapper]` tag ("launches a child process") also drags the JSON-contract rows (PROC-07/19/20/21/22, BIN-26 README sentences about a pin) onto a pager and a dev script. PROC-17 and the SecureString ban hit the legitimate adapter and prompt APIs of a CLI framework, and the legacy-TFM fallbacks (PROC-01/09/14) are RS0030 errors in the tag-blind ban file.

Gate defects found by experiment (F6-F8, F13): the PROC-01 wiring cell goes green while a nested Directory.Build.targets keeps the ban file out of the build (CommandLineUtils: 0 RS0030 before the nested file imported the root one, 11 after); P9 counts files, not launch sites; P13 misses `return p?.StandardInput ?? x` and `Use(p.StandardInput)`; eng/triangulate.py exits 0 on a pin file with wrong digests and on a duplicate manifest row.

Claims checked against the ban files and found faithful: PROC-01/02/06/09/11/14/17 symbol sets, BIN-10 (24 ExtractToDirectory lines), BIN-11 (12 for the four named plus LoadIntoBufferAsync, GetFromJson, ReadFromJson), BIN-16 (4 symbols plus CA5359 and SYSLIB0014 at error in analyzers.globalconfig).

Harness caveats (not rule defects): fixtures/.globalconfig is a stray copy of analyzers.globalconfig that puts CA* at error for every tree under fixtures, so builds fail on CA errors and report MultipleGlobalAnalyzerKeys if a tree adds its own; I used -p:EnableNETAnalyzers=false. Known organic causes recurred and are not new: OpenSSL SHA1 strong-name failure on CommandLineUtils (SignAssembly=false), and MinVer on a blob-less checkout (markdig, '..0.0' AssemblyVersion). heldout3-tmp holds other agents' temp dirs and was left alone; none of my cells uses mktemp, and my scratch dirs there are removed. global.json: markdig `src/global.json` (10.0.100, latestMinor) rolled to 10.0.401; Ocelot's only sets the test runner. Nothing was mishandled by the skills or rules.

failures.class: No sanctioned form for a legitimate use
failures.problem: No row names a form for an optional, interactive, terminal-inheriting child launched by an OS-utility name: the Pager (less) redirects only stdin, resolves by bare name from PATH, waits without a bound for the user to quit, catches every start failure to fall back to the console, and exposes Kill(). PROC-02 (redirect all three streams), PROC-03/BIN-01 (rooted resolver result), PROC-09 and PROC-15 (no sync wait, always a timeout) and PROC-05 (only catch Win32Exception) each demand the opposite, and redirecting stdout would break the pager.
failures.evidence: src/CommandLineUtils/IO/Pager.cs lines 118-176. P9 prints 4 MISSING lines for it (CreateNoWindow, WorkingDirectory, RedirectStandardOutput, RedirectStandardError); c02 prints lines 120-122 (FileName = "less"); P16 prints MISSING Kill(entireProcessTree) and MISSING timeout source; P3 prints the file, though the hazard is unreachable because `_enabled = !IsOSPlatform(Windows)`; RS0030 fires on Kill() (101) and WaitForExit() (174).
failures.fix: Add one sanctioned-form clause: a user-facing interactive child (pager, editor) may inherit stdout/stderr, may be named by its OS utility name with a degrade-to-plain-output catch, and may wait for the user without a timeout, if the file says so in a same-line comment; P9 and P16 exempt a seam carrying that comment.

failures.problem: The tag `[cli-wrapper]` is defined as `the library launches a child process` (index Tags) but the family says it owns `a wrapped command-line tool` and is silent on a tree that starts none. A pager, a git rev-parse helper or a dev oracle script is bound by the rows that presuppose the reference tool's JSON contract (`--format json` composer, `exit_code` error document, handshake contract table, transient-75 retry) and by BIN-26 README sentences about what a pin proves.
failures.evidence: On CommandLineUtils c04 (PROC-07, must print exactly one line) prints 0, c16 (PROC-19, must print exactly one path) prints 0, G4 prints empty `==` sections; G4 also prints empty sections on markdig. markdig tools/GfmTableDifferential and the Pager are both bound by the whole family under the index definition.
failures.fix: Split the tag: `[cli-wrapper]` for a library whose purpose is wrapping one tool, a lighter tag for any child launch (binding only PROC-01, 09, 11, 12, 14), and a `[json-cli]` tag for PROC-07 and PROC-19 to PROC-22 and the BIN-26 pin sentences; make the index definition and the family header agree.

failures.class: No sanctioned form for a legitimate use
failures.problem: PROC-17 is [library] and bans Console.CancelKeyPress with no sanctioned form, but CommandLineUtils is a CLI framework that owns the application lifetime: IConsole/PhysicalConsole forward a caller's subscription (add => Console.CancelKeyPress += value), CommandLineApplication.ExecuteAsync adds and removes a scoped Ctrl+C handler, and Hosting.CommandLine installs e.Cancel = true. BIN-16 sanctions a forwarded caller-supplied callback; PROC-17 does not. The ban also fires on an XML-doc cref, and misses the real installs because they go through the IConsole interface.
failures.evidence: RS0030 CS-PROC-17 at PhysicalConsole.cs(26,24) (a `<see cref="Console.CancelKeyPress"/>` comment), (30,20) and (35,21); CommandLineApplication.cs:923,931 and CommandLineLifetime.cs:84 install handlers through IConsole and are not reported.
failures.fix: State that a console-adapter that only forwards the caller's subscription, and a framework whose job is hosting the app lifetime, are the sanctioned form (same wording as BIN-16's forwarded callback); say the cell must not count XML-doc crefs.

failures.problem: Line 203 bans T:System.Security.SecureString and attributes it to CS-PROC-08, but the PROC-08 row never mentions SecureString; the owner is security.md (H17). A public password-prompt API that returns SecureString (CommandLineUtils Prompt.GetPasswordAsSecureString, existing for consumers of X509 and Process password APIs) has no sanctioned route, and the reader of PROC-08 cannot find the rule the build message cites.
failures.evidence: RS0030 CS-PROC-08 at Prompt.cs(129,32), (136,25), (136,47), (139,25), (144,13) in the net8.0 build; `rg SecureString rules/csharp-quality/processes.md` returns nothing, security.md lines 72, 176, 179 own the ban.
failures.fix: Re-attribute the ban line to the security.md row, and give that row a sanctioned form for a public prompt/credential-API return type.

failures.problem: The legacy-TFM fallbacks the rows mandate (write ProcessStartInfo.Arguments through one quoting helper; root-only Kill(); sync WaitForExit(ms) on a pool thread) are exactly the symbols BannedSymbols.txt bans at RS0030 error, and the ban file is not tag-aware. The rows state no pragma form for the fallback, so a net472 leg cannot comply and stay green, while the rows say [greenfield] alone binds the preferred form.
failures.evidence: CommandLineUtils (net8.0;net472) Pager.cs(123,21) Arguments, (101,29) Kill(), (174,13) WaitForExit(): all RS0030 errors in the build, while the code is the sanctioned fallback shape (ArgumentEscaper.EscapeAndConcatenate quoting helper).
failures.fix: In each of the three rows state that the fallback line carries `#pragma warning disable RS0030` with a same-line reason inside the one seam, as PROC-09 already does for its two exceptions, and that the ban file is the greenfield posture.

failures.problem: The wiring cell (`rg -l -U -e '<AdditionalFiles[^>]*BannedSymbols...' -g '*.targets' ... .`) proves only that some file contains the text. A nested Directory.Build.targets shadows the root one (MSBuild reads the nearest only), so the cell prints a path and the ban is inert. Gate wiring false-green, the exact class G the file lists.
failures.evidence: CommandLineUtils has src/Directory.Build.targets. With the ban registered in the root Directory.Build.targets, c00 printed ./Directory.Build.targets, `dotnet msbuild -getItem:AdditionalFiles` showed only PublicAPI.*.txt, and the build reported 0 RS0030 for Pager.cs (Kill(), Arguments, WaitForExit all banned). After the nested file imported the root one: 64 RS0030, 11 of them CS-PROC.
failures.fix: Replace the text match with a per-shipped-project proof: `dotnet msbuild "$PRJ" -p:TargetFramework=<tfm> -getItem:AdditionalFiles` must list BannedSymbols.txt for every shipped project, or require the canary to be the only wiring proof.

failures.problem: P9 counts seam files and tests the six members per file, not per launch site. Two ProcessStartInfo creations in one file pass the count, and a member present at one site masks its absence at the other.
failures.evidence: tools/GfmTableDifferential/Program.cs creates `new ProcessStartInfo("git") { RedirectStandardOutput = true }` (line 18) and `new ProcessStartInfo(exe, ...)` (line 34, with CreateNoWindow, input and error redirects). P9 reports only `MISSING UseShellExecute` and `MISSING WorkingDirectory`; it prints no `found 2` and does not report that the git site lacks CreateNoWindow, RedirectStandardInput and RedirectStandardError.
failures.fix: Count creation sites per project (rg -c on the P0 patterns, or one -o per match) and print `expected exactly 1 seam site per tool`; check the six members within the statement that contains each creation, not anywhere in the file.

failures.problem: P13 recognises only `= ...StandardInput` aliases and direct `.Write*` calls. A getter or argument that hands the child's StandardInput TextWriter to a caller (`return x?.StandardInput ?? fallback`, `Use(p.StandardInput)`) with no StandardInputEncoding set is the same hazard and is not printed.
failures.evidence: Pager.cs `return _less.Value?.StandardInput ?? _fallbackWriter;` and the whole-tree run print nothing for P13. A planted set of 8 one-line variants: P13 printed `var w = p.StandardInput;`, `p.StandardInput.WriteLine(x)`, `.Write(x)` and `TextWriter W => p.StandardInput;`, and missed `return p?.StandardInput;`, `return p.Value?.StandardInput ?? fb;` and `Use(p.StandardInput);`. (P3 catches the Pager under PROC-11, so the gate still reds, but P13 is the cell PROC-12 cites.)
failures.fix: Match every `\bStandardInput\b` not followed by `.BaseStream`, `.Dispose` or `.Close` in a file with no `StandardInputEncoding`.

failures.problem: The first alternative of the PROC-11 cell flags any `Standard*Encoding = Encoding.*`, including StandardOutputEncoding and StandardErrorEncoding, but the stated hazard (a BOM preamble emitted on a pipe) exists only for StandardInputEncoding; a decoder handed Encoding.UTF8 is harmless. The row text 'never assign an Encoding.* member to a Standard*Encoding property' over-reaches its own rationale and the cell fires on code that is correct.
failures.evidence: tools/GfmTableDifferential/Program.cs:34 `StandardInputEncoding = new UTF8Encoding(false), StandardOutputEncoding = Encoding.UTF8`: c09 prints the line although the input side is already the shared no-BOM form.
failures.fix: Restrict the Encoding.* ban pattern to StandardInputEncoding (and a StreamWriter over a pipe); keep 'one shared Utf8NoBom on all three' as a style SHOULD for the output side.

failures.problem: The cell uses `rg -i -e 'curl '` with no word boundary, so any identifier ending in `...cUrl ` followed by a space matches (GetDynamicUrl, PublicUrl, StaticUrl, GenericUrl).
failures.evidence: markdig src/Markdig prod scope: 5 false positives in 3 files (LinkInline.cs:150,153, LinkInlineRenderer.cs:28, AutoIdentifierExtension.cs:134,136), the only c29 hits in that tree.
failures.fix: Use `\bcurl\b` case-sensitively, or `-w -e curl`, and scope with `ProcessStartInfo`/`FileName` proximity as G1 does.

failures.problem: SRC means two things. processes.md and the index define it as the space-separated product source directories, used unquoted (`$SRC`); binaries.md reads it quoted as one directory (`"${SRC:?MISSING SRC}"`, 'SRC is the shipped source directory'). Set once per repository as the index tells it, a repository with two product directories passes the PROC cells and makes every quoted BIN cell exit 2.
failures.evidence: SRC="src tools" on markdig: c19-c35, G1 and G3 (and G2's helper line) all printed `rg: src tools: IO error ... No such file or directory`, exit 2, while c01-c18 and P1-P16 ran. CommandLineUtils has three product directories (CommandLineUtils, Hosting.CommandLine, CommandLineUtils.Generators).
failures.fix: Make binaries.md cells use unquoted `$SRC` / `$INSTALL_DIR` (with the guard) like processes.md, or define SRC and INSTALL_DIR once in the index as a single directory or a list and say which.

failures.rule_id: Conventions test-exclusion glob (processes.md:41-43, every PROC cell)
failures.problem: Three different test-exclusion globs ship: processes.md keeps the substring `!**/*[Tt]est*/**` that round 2 decision 2 retired, binaries.md uses `{[Tt]est,[Tt]ests,*.[Tt]est,*.[Tt]ests,*Tests,*TestFixtures,*TestServices}`, and the index lists `[Tt]est`, `[Tt]ests`, `*Test`, `*Tests`, `*TestFixtures`, `*TestServices`. The index says every family file copies the glob. Test directories named for the style rather than the word (unit, acceptance) are caught by neither and the two families disagree on testing/.
failures.evidence: Ocelot has unit/, acceptance/, testing/ test projects. Whole-tree run: the PROC glob drops testing/ but scans unit/ and acceptance/ (P8 prints unit/Middleware/OcelotMiddlewareExtensionsTests.cs:346; c13 prints acceptance/WebSockets/*.cs); the BIN glob scans all three (c23 69 vs 9 hits, c34 34 vs 5, c35 46 vs 12, c26 14 vs 3 for whole tree vs src).
failures.fix: Define the glob once in the index (including the 'add your test directory' line as a variable such as TESTDIRS), and have both families interpolate it instead of retyping it.

failures.problem: The refresh gate is documented to exit 1 on any disagreement and to be run on every change to the pin file, but it reads only the pin file's triple keys: the pin digests and the pin `version` are never compared with the agreed sources, and a duplicate (version, filename) manifest row is resolved last-wins, so a poisoned first row is hidden.
failures.evidence: Synthetic inputs: genuine pins exit 0 `rows 2 mismatches 0`; a pin file with the right triples and one wrong digest (`c`x64 for an `a`x64 source) exits 0 `mismatches 0`; a manifest with a poisoned duplicate row listed first exits 0; a pin `version` 0.9 against 1.0 exits 0. The pin jq gate also passes the wrong-digest file (it checks shape only).
failures.fix: After the three sources agree, compare `pins[target] == agreed digest` for every row and `pinfile.version == ver`, and fail on any duplicate (version, target, filename) row in the manifest or the checksum file.

failures.problem: G4 hard-codes the root file name `README.md` (case-sensitive), prints the root name twice when PackageReadmeFile is also README.md, and then matches `-g "**/$f"` at any depth, so a trust sentence in any README.md under the tree (a docs or samples one) satisfies it.
failures.evidence: CsvHelper's root readme is README.markdown: G4 prints an empty `== README.md` section as if missing and never looks at the real file. markdig's lowercase `readme.md` is seen only through PackageReadmeFile. CommandLineUtils and Ocelot print `== README.md` twice.
failures.fix: Resolve the readme the same way the pack does (PackageReadmeFile, else `README*` at the repository root, case-insensitive), `sort -u` the loop list and anchor the glob to that path.

failures.problem: Conventions says the family `is silent on a tree that starts no wrapped tool`, and P9 follows it (prints nothing), but the seam-dependent cells fail on such a tree with a stderr-only `MISSING seam files` and exit 1 (stdout stays empty, which the file defines as a pass). P11 does the same with `MISSING caller token parameter` on a tree whose seams take no token.
failures.evidence: CsvHelper, Ocelot and markdig-src: c18, P11, P14, P16 all exit 1 with `f: MISSING seam files` on stderr and empty stdout. CommandLineUtils: P11 `n: MISSING caller token parameter` on stderr, empty stdout.
failures.fix: Have the seam finder return success with an explicit `no seam: family silent` line on stdout when none exists, and keep the MISSING failure for a tree that declares the tag; print MISSING messages to stdout so the 'empty is pass' rule cannot swallow them.

report:
Round 3 sweep of rules/csharp-quality/security.md and observability.md on markdig, CsvHelper, CommandLineUtils (CLU) and Ocelot. Result: 14 failures, all instances of known classes. No new class and no new MUST.

SETUP
- Ran about 85 cell commands across 8 fenced blocks (5 gate and grep blocks, 4 pack, build-code and registry blocks, plus the licences script) on 4 trees, about 340 cell-tree runs.
- Greps ran verbatim with SRC and TESTS set per tree. Dotnet cells ran on SDK 10.0.401 against copies. The pack, build-code, licences and registry blocks needed eng/*.txt operand files, which I created empty in my copies.
- I also installed the shipped posture on each tree's lead project (BannedSymbols.txt, BannedSymbols.Src.txt and analyzers.globalconfig, BannedApi analyzers 5.6.0, 10.0-all) and built net8.0. That compares the grep cells with the real RS0030/CA diagnostics.
- Environment hazard, not a rule failure: /home/mherwig/.cache/research-lang/dotnet-tools/fixtures/ contains a .globalconfig (the shipped analyzers.globalconfig), a .editorconfig and a global.json. Roslyn discovers .globalconfig upward, so every tree copied under fixtures/ got the posture (CA1307 and CA1062 errors on plain pack).
- I moved my working copy to /home/mherwig/.cache/research-lang/h3-sec/ (80 MB). Anyone else running trees under fixtures/ is affected.
- heldout3-tmp is shared with ~60 live dotnet processes. I removed only dead-pid pipes and 2 empty dirs. My MSBuildTemp leftovers there cannot be told apart from other agents' and remain.

CELL RESULTS (hits per tree: markdig / CsvHelper / CLU / Ocelot)
- OBS greps:
  - CS-OBS-02: 0 / 0 / 2 / 86
  - CS-OBS-06: 0 / 0 / 0 / 4
  - CS-OBS-11: 0 / 0 / 1 / 18
  - CS-OBS-12: 0 / 0 / 0 / 70
  - CS-OBS-13: 0 / 0 / 4 / 5
  - CS-OBS-15: 0 / 0 / 1 / 0
  - Every other OBS cell printed nothing.
  - No tree has an ActivitySource, Meter, scope, IProgress, traceparent or log-then-rethrow. CS-OBS-17..24 and 26..29 therefore had no subject here, so those rules were not exercised.
- OBS-02 reading:
  - CLU's 2 hits are true positives. They are MEL extension calls in Hosting.CommandLine, and the analyzer agrees.
  - Ocelot's 86 hits are all false positives (finding 7).
  - OBS-06 on Ocelot: the 1 hit (4 lines) is a true positive.
  - OBS-12 on Ocelot: all 70 hits are false positives.
  - OBS-13 on CLU and Ocelot, and OBS-15 on CLU: true positives except the over-broad Microsoft.Extensions pattern (finding 8).
- SEC greps:
  - CS-SEC-03 cmd 1: 0 / 0 / 0 / 1.
  - CS-SEC-03 cmd 2: 0 / 8 / 0 / 5.
  - CS-SEC-05: 0 / 1 / 2 / 10.
  - CS-SEC-08: only Ocelot, 2 hits.
  - CS-SEC-04 and CS-SEC-06: nothing anywhere.
  - CS-SEC-07 and CS-SEC-16: nothing anywhere.
- SEC-03 reading:
  - CsvHelper's 8 hits are true positives and match the 8 RS0030 errors exactly. The inputs are mostly developer constants, but the rule's instruction is right.
  - Ocelot cmd 1 is a true positive: RegexGlobal sets REGEX_DEFAULT_MATCH_TIMEOUT via AppDomain.SetData in a static constructor, which the rule forbids and whose rationale (a late set is ignored) applies.
  - Ocelot cmd 2: 2 true positives (static Regex.Match at UrlPathPlaceholderNameAndValueFinder.cs:66 and :75), 3 false positives (finding 1).
- SEC-05 reading:
  - CsvHelper's DataTable in CsvDataReader.GetSchemaTable (implements IDataReader) is legitimate.
  - CLU's SecureString is a public Prompt API.
  - Ocelot's 10 Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration usings are its integration surface. One of them is a trailing comment at IInternalConfiguration.cs:4, a false positive. See finding 3.
- SEC-08 reading: both Ocelot hits are true positives (MD5Helper cache key, SHA1 rate-limit storage key). The instruction is right: SHA-256 would serve, and CA5350 and CA5351 do fire.
- Gate and pack blocks:
  - CS-SEC-01 prints every project on all 4 trees, as expected for a tree that has not adopted the posture.
  - CS-SEC-02: no duplicates. The .globalconfig check printed MISSING-OPERAND, and the canary path raised MSB1009 (loud, named).
  - CS-SEC-09/10 printed the runtime dependencies only because my owner file was empty. Each pair is right: markdig and CsvHelper list System.Memory, Microsoft.Bcl.* and Microsoft.CSharp, and Ocelot lists 5 packages on 3 TFMs.
  - CS-SEC-12 printed UNVERIFIED for 5 markdig and 4 Ocelot packages, by design.
  - CS-SEC-13 printed ipaddressrange 6.3.0 MPL-2.0, a human decision by design.
  - CS-SEC-14 and CS-SEC-15 behaved: three trees have no dependabot.yml, and CLU's cooldown awk exits 1 silently (the row says it exits 0).
- Posture build (RS0030 and CA diagnostics, net8.0):
  - markdig: none for security or logging.
  - CsvHelper: 8 CS-SEC-03.
  - CLU: 47 CS-OBS-16, 5 CS-PROC-08 (SecureString), 2 CS-SEC-04, plus other families.
  - Ocelot: 2 CS-SEC-03, 1 CS-BIN-16, 2 CA5359 (error), CA5350 (error, SHA1), CA5351 (warning, MD5).
  - CLU Hosting.CommandLine, built separately against its project reference: CA1848 on 4 sites, CA1873 on 2, CA1727 on 2.

FAILURES (all known=true)
1. CS-SEC-03 cmd 2 false positive on a positional GeneratedRegex timeout (Ocelot).
2. CS-SEC-04 cmd false negative on a wrapped Type.GetType call (CLU). RS0030 backstops it at build.
3. CS-SEC-05: no carve-out for IConfiguration integration surfaces, IDataReader implementers or SecureString API compatibility. Also a trailing-comment false positive.
4. CS-SEC-01, CS-SEC-06 and CS-SEC-02 (CA5359): an operator-opt-in "accept any certificate" feature has no sanctioned form (Ocelot).
5. Silent Hazards H18 / CS-SEC-02 / CS-SEC-05: CA5359 does fire on the `=> true` forms the row calls silent.
6. SecureString ban message cites CS-PROC-08 while the rows cite CS-SEC-05. The ban applies to non-consumers, and the row is tagged [consumer].
7. CS-OBS-02, CS-OBS-06, CS-OBS-12: false positives on a library-owned logging facade, and the instruction cannot apply to it (Ocelot IOcelotLogger).
8. CS-OBS-02 and CS-OBS-06 false negative on `logger?.LogX(` (CLU, Ocelot). CS-OBS-13 (a) and (b) over-broad on Microsoft.Extensions.* (CLU Hosting, Ocelot).
9. CS-OBS-16: no sanctioned form for a library whose product is console I/O (CLU).
10. CS-SEC-11 and CS-SEC-13 hard-code obj/project.assets.json (CLU relocates obj to .build/obj).
11. The pack blocks fail verbatim on a project with GeneratePackageOnBuild (Ocelot, NU5026).
12. CS-OBS-11 noise: the cell scans `.` and hits samples, tests and benchmarks only.
13. CS-OBS-08: no definition of application versus library for an ASP.NET middleware framework (Ocelot logs Information per request in 15 sites across 21 middlewares).

RULES JUDGED RIGHT FOR THESE TREES
- CS-SEC-03: right even where the input is a developer constant.
- CS-SEC-07: right, no hits.
- CS-SEC-08: right.
- CS-SEC-09 and CS-SEC-10 mechanism: right.
- CS-SEC-12 and CS-SEC-13 mechanism: right.
- CS-OBS-01, CS-OBS-04, CS-OBS-05 and CS-OBS-14: right. The analyzers flagged lowercase placeholders (CA1727) and a string.Join argument (CA1873) on CLU Hosting.

Scratch is at /home/mherwig/.cache/research-lang/h3-sec/ (cell instrumentation in _inst/, outputs in _out/, posture builds in _posture/). The working copies of the 4 trees live there too.

failures.problem: Cell 2 (the Regex-without-timeout grep) flags [GeneratedRegex(pattern, options, <positional ms constant>)] because it only accepts an argument that contains the words timespan, timeout or nonbacktracking. The row documents only the named form matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 1000.
failures.evidence: 3 false positives at src/DownstreamRouteFinder/UrlMatcher/UrlPathPlaceholderNameAndValueFinder.cs:44, :103 and :120 ([GeneratedRegex(@..., RegexOptions.None, PlaceholdersMilliseconds)] with a const of 1000/300/300). The posture build raised no RS0030 for them. It raised RS0030 only for the two real static Regex.Match calls at lines 66 and 75. The same file's RegexGlobal.DefaultMatchTimeoutMilliseconds callers pass only because the identifier contains 'Timeout'.

(d) NN `CS-ASYNC-14` states an unconditional ban, while async.md owns an allowlist with reason for sync contracts the library does not own; CLU `CommandLineApplication.Execute()` calls `ExecuteAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult()` as a public sync entry, and Ocelot's TimerCallback poller does the same.

failures.problem: The NOT RUN loop uses grep -qE "[(]$t[|)]". In zsh (the default tool shell) $t[|)] is parsed as an array subscript, so sourcing the block aborts with `invalid subscript`. Everything after it, including the tag decision and the `S1: red baseline, no tag` message, never runs and prints nothing. The agent sees no tag line either way.
failures.evidence: upg-00.sh:12: invalid subscript (zsh); `zsh -c 't=net8.0; echo "[(]$t[|)]"'` -> (eval):2: invalid subscript; bash prints the pattern. No pre-net10 tag and no S1 line were printed.
failures.fix: Quote or brace the variable ("[(]${t}[|)]") and/or tell the agent to run blocks under bash; make the tail print an explicit result line on every path.
